match.reason: The closest bank point explains why Australia runs deficits through saving and income outflows, but it does not cover the cyclical movement from commodity prices that the new point's brief asks for, so it is broader in coverage than a clean match.

draft.title: The current account balance
card: The current account balance is the sum of the balance on goods and services, net primary income and net secondary income. A deficit means money flowing out is greater than money flowing in.
Australia usually runs a current account deficit. The main cause is a deficit on net primary income, which is mostly interest and dividends paid to overseas investors.
short-run swings that move the balance from year to year. Commodity prices are one example: higher export prices raise export income and narrow the deficit.

long-run features of the economy that keep a deficit in place. Low national saving is one example, because Australia relies on foreign funds to pay for investment, and income is then paid to foreign owners.
draft.remember: Cyclical influences move the balance year to year. Structural ones keep the deficit there.

a.q: Which of these is a cyclical influence on Australia's current account balance?
opts: A fall in the world price of iron ore
Low national saving over many decades
A long-run reliance on foreign funds
Ongoing income payments to foreign investors
a.why: A change in commodity prices comes and goes with the world economy, so it moves the balance from year to year. The other three are long-run features of the economy, so they are structural, not cyclical.
a.clue: Which one can change quickly from one year to the next?

b.q: Australia's export prices for coal rise sharply for a year, and the current account deficit narrows. Why does the deficit return to its usual level later?
opts: Structural influences such as low saving remain in place
Higher coal prices are a structural influence that fades
Cyclical influences keep the deficit in place over time
Exports are not counted in the current account balance
b.why: The coal price rise is a cyclical influence, so its effect is temporary. Structural influences such as low saving and income paid overseas stay in place, so the deficit tends to return. Exports are counted in the balance on goods and services.
b.clue: Which type of influence lasts, and which one passes?

a.best: A fall in the world price of iron ore

b.best: Structural influences such as low saving remain in place
